column1: # The models that .github/scripts/formal.py runs (AUD-5, #389): <name> <files> <what it is> [<slices>], separated by tabs.
# The files are paths below tests/formal, joined in this order into one ProVerif input, which formal.py runs
# with the pinned ProVerif (.github/scripts/formal.py run). The queries of the files are numbered by their
# (* @query id *) comments, and expected.tsv says what each must give in each variant. A line that starts
# A session model is the session of alice with bob, the compromises of one scenario, and the groups of queries that the
# scenario is about: q-reach (the handshake can complete), q-secrecy, q-authserver, q-authclient, q-negotiation and
# q-replay. Where the attacker holds the Noise key of the server the queries of the client (q-authclient) and of replay
# are left out: there the attacker is the server, and what ProVerif would have to do is to prove a long list of attacks
# false one by one. The scenarios, by the keys that the attacker holds: none; cert (the key of the certificate of the
# server); cert-client (that and the Noise key of the client); noise-client (the Noise keys of the server and of the
# client); both (both keys of the server); noise (the Noise key of the server); fs (every key, after the sessions).
# slices: ProVerif keeps its state for every query of a run, so a variant with many queries runs as that many
# ProVerif runs, each with consecutive queries of its own and a job of its own in formal.yml. 1 when the column is
# The session over TLS 1.3 on TCP 443, as the code has it
